transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-11
Start: 20:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Evan Park (HarborTel Platform), Sofia Martinez (HarborTel SRE), Rashid Alvi (HarborTel CTO)

Summary (auto): quick sync to validate throughput profile changes and plan handover.

[00:00] Liam: ok, hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick note on agenda — priya will walk through the new continuous-batching profile we tested overnight, then we'll go over the soak plan and the handover checklist. any blockers up front?

[00:22] Evan: no blockers, just wanted to confirm the target — we're shooting for 600 qps steady with a p99 < 220ms, is that still the target?

[00:30] Priya: yes that's right, the 600 qps at 220 p99 is the goal for the external-facing inference path. we also scoped an internal lower-latency path for admin flows.

[00:45] Sofia: quick caveat — our traffic has burstiness every 3 hours from batch jobs, so queueing behavior matters as much as average. we've seen tail hiccups in previous runs.

[01:02] Priya: understood. for that we adjusted the continuous-batching thresholds — smaller max-batch size but more aggressive batch-timeouts and a soft-priority lane for short requests. that reduces head-of-line blocking.

[01:28] Liam: priya, can you say more about the 'soft-priority lane'? i'm hearing that you split small short requests into a separate queue so kv-cache warmup isn't delayed?

[01:37] Priya: exactly. it's basically two logical queues in the serving runtime: the main batcher (throughput optimized) and a low-latency fast-path. requests under 64 tokens go to the fast-path which has lower batching window (like 3ms) and preemptive dispatch. larger requests get into the throughput batch where we allow up to 64 concurrent inflight in the pool.

[01:55] Evan: hmm that sounds promising. what's the impact on GPU utilization? last week our utilization dropped with the smaller batches.

[02:05] Priya: tradeoff — you lose a bit of utilization, but because we use prefix/KV caching and shard-aware routing the net tokens/sec stayed within 95% of prior peaks. we measured ~6% throughput loss but tail p99 improved by ~30-40%.

[02:24] Rashid: 6% throughput loss could matter for cost. do you have a cost delta figure? hosted vs dedicated?

[02:33] Liam: we ran an estimate last night — for your baseline traffic the 6% extra cost on hosted is roughly $1.2k/month in our model, but with a 4-GPU Dedicated pool you can absorb that and still be ~12% cheaper at your committed loads. i'll share the spreadsheet.

[02:52] Sofia: can you also show failure modes? like what happens if queue depth spikes and we hit backpressure?

[03:00] Priya: yes. we configured three fallback tiers: 1) fast-path degrade (reduce max tokens in batch), 2) model-variant fallback to a smaller quantized model for non-critical routes, 3) region fallback to alternate cluster. We tested scenario A in the sim — when qdepth > 1200 we start shedding non-essential traffic and prioritize admin/low-latency lanes.

[03:27] Evan: model fallback worries me — we rely on consistent outputs for reranking. if we fallback to quantized model that may change scores. how do we detect quality regressions?

[03:38] Priya: good point. the platform tags fallback outputs and we run a lightweight recalibration step on the host side — we also keep a small sample of inputs for continuous evals. Pragmatically, we only enable model variant fallback for low-risk routes and revert automatically when latency stabilizes.

[03:58] Liam: action item — we'll include the fallback tag in the response header so you can measure delta on your side.

[04:07] Sofia: lovely. on soak testing — what exactly should we capture? p50/p95/p99, nvprof traces, queue histograms?

[04:15] Priya: full list: p50/p90/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth over time, batch size distribution, KV-cache hit rates, and sample latencies per request size. plus a few end-to-end traces for errors. we'll provide the profilers and a script to collect queue histograms.

[04:36] Evan: timeline — we can start the 24h soak tomorrow if we have access to the Dedicated test cluster. provisioning might take a day.

[04:43] Liam: understood. evan — can you confirm provisioning ETA?

[04:49] Evan: i'll try to get infra to spin up 4xA100 by Wednesday morning, so should be able to begin the soak by then.

[05:00] Priya: for the Dedicated handover checklist: 1) access and roles (SSO/LDAP), 2) VPC peering and NAT egress plan, 3) KMS key exchange for model artifacts, 4) monitoring hooks and alerting thresholds. we put a draft runbook in the shared drive — link posted in chat.

[05:24] Rashid: security items — we need SOC2 evidence and log retention details for audit. who owns that?

[05:31] Liam: Redwood's security team will send SOC2 and architecture diagrams — i'll follow up with an email. we can also enable audit logs at token-level for Dedicated if you need longer retention.

[05:45] Sofia: on the queue shaping parameters you showed earlier — what did you use for rate shaping constants? I remember gamma = 0.9 in earlier sim but that caused oscillation.

[05:56] Priya: we moved to a conservative alpha of 0.65 and a smoothing window of 12s for the token arrival estimator. that reduced oscillation; we also clamp growth to avoid cascading scale events.

[06:12] Evan: interesting. do you have replay scripts so we can reproduce the spike patterns?

[06:18] Priya: yes, replay harness is in the repo. it can replay production traces with configurable burstiness and ramp rate. we'll push an annotated trace that replicates your every-3-hour batch job pattern.

[06:35] Liam: ok, quick recap of decisions: Redwood will send tuned batching config, profiler scripts, and cost/hosted-vs-dedicated spreadsheet. HarborTel will provision the Dedicated test cluster and run a 24h soak with the provided scripts. both sides will reconvene after soak to review traces and decide on handover.

[06:56] Sofia: sounds good. one more thought — can we get a sample of the KV-cache warmup script? cold-starts were a pain earlier.

[07:05] Priya: yes, i'm packaging a warmup script that primes common prefixes and uses a weighted replay so it doesn't thrash the cluster. will include example cron job.

[07:18] Rashid: anything else about SLOs? we wanted a plan for error budget consumption during ramp.

[07:24] Liam: propose a staged SLO ramp: week 0 (test) 75% traffic, week 1 90%, week 2 100%. if p99 exceeds 250ms in any window >30m we'll roll back a stage. we'll document in the runbook.

[07:42] Evan: ok that gives us a safety net. thanks.

[07:48] Liam: thanks all. we'll action items — priya, you have the profiling exports and plays. priy a?

[07:55] Priya: yep i'll get traces out by Saturday.

[08:00] Liam: closing notes: scheduled follow-up for Monday 2027-03-15 16:00 UTC to review soak results. i'll send calendar invite.

[08:10] Sofia: thanks everyone.

[08:12] Rashid: thanks.

[08:14] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and dropped punctuation; speakers sometimes overlap. Some technical terms transcribed verbatim but acronyms like KV, SLO, SOC2 clipped or spelled out inconsistently.
